title: Tor interval of an algebraic local finite-quotient model
statement: Let X be a scheme, (A,I) an adic coefficient datum and M an arbitrary derived object over its completed coefficient sheaf. Let phi be isomorphisms from the constant finite quotient rings to the actual finite coefficient sheaves, satisfying both compatibility equations [def-weil-pbc-finite-perfect-quotient-model-data]. Fix an etale chart V and integers a,b, and assume the residue reduction has etale-local constant finite-projective models in [a,b]. For any n, any W->V, and any algebraic A/I^(n+1)-complex P, suppose either W is nonempty or P is zero. If the actual nth reduction of M and the changed constant realization of P become isomorphic after actual derived restriction to W, then Q(P) has Tor amplitude [a,b]: tensor with every A/I^(n+1)-module in degree zero has cohomology zero outside that interval. P need not have finite terms, bounded terms, or projective terms.

source.place: Tags 094I (lemma-bounded, coefficient ideal filtration) and 094G (lemma-locally-constant); proetale.tex Tag 09C2 (lemma-describe-constructible-complexes)

proof.text: If P is zero as a complex, Q(P) is zero since localization preserves zero objects. For each module N, tensorRight(N[0]) preserves zero objects, so Q(P) tensor-derived N[0] has zero cohomology in every degree. This proves the conclusion on the zero-complex alternative, including empty charts.

On the nonempty-chart alternative apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-quotient-model-residue-projective]. With B = A/I^(n+1) and J the image of I in B, obtain a universal derived scalar extension L to B/J and a projective complex E in [a,b] representing L(Q(P)). Only the residue complex, not Q(P), has been replaced by a bounded projective model here.

The image ideal J satisfies J^(n+1) = image(I^(n+1)) = 0. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nilpotent-projective-complex-lift] to B, J, the universal derived extension L with its counit, Q(P), and E. It gives a projective complex F representing Q(P), together with a complex isomorphism F tensor_B B/J = E. For any module T whose scalar extension is zero, the tensor-quotient identification gives T/JT = 0. Thus T = JT, and induction gives T = J^m T for every m. Taking m = n+1 gives T = 0. Apply this to F^i whenever E^i = 0, so F is strictly supported in [a,b], retaining both original endpoints.

source.place: Tag 09AR, lemma-lift-complex-projectives; nilpotent Nakayama argument as in Tag 00DV

proof.text: Every projective term of F is flat. The generic bounded-flat Tor theorem [lem-trf-source-bounded-flat-tor-amplitude] makes Q(F) have Tor amplitude [a,b]. Transport it through the supplied isomorphism Q(F) = Q(P), using invariance of Tor amplitude under isomorphisms. No hypothesis on the finite generation of P or of a tensor test module is introduced.

proof_origin.place: Tag 094I, residue identification, followed by the alternative projective-lifting argument of Tag 09AR and bounded-flat Tor amplitude

lean.statement:
theorem finiteQuotient_model_torAmplitude
    (X : Scheme.{t}) {A : Type t} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A)
    [∀ n : ℕ, (koszulConstantFunctor X (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1))).PreservesZeroMorphisms]
    (φ : ∀ n : ℕ, adicConstantRing X (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1)) ⟶
      completedAdicFiniteCommRing X d n)
    (hφ : ∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (φ n)) (hcompat : FinitePerfectModelsCompatible X d φ)
    (M : DerivedCategory (CompletedAdicModules X d)) (V : X.Etale) (a b : ℤ)
    (hresidue : FinitePerfectModelsOn X d φ M 0 V a b)
    (n : ℕ) (W : X.Etale) (g : W ⟶ V)
    (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{t} (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1))) ℤ)
    (hchart : Nonempty W.left ∨ IsZero P)
    (e : Nonempty
      (ringedSiteDerivedRestrictionOfUniverses (completedAdicFiniteRing X d n)
          ((toProEt X).obj W) ((completedAdicQuotientReduction X d n).obj M) ≅
        ringedSiteDerivedRestrictionOfUniverses (completedAdicFiniteRing X d n)
          ((toProEt X).obj W) ((completedAdicDerivedChange X (φ n)).obj
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (finiteModelConstantComplex X _ P))))) :
    DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn (ModuleCat.{t} (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1))) a b
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)
